title: Fix first-pass approval percent rendered 100x too large in both IDE clients
description: Producer packages/moe-daemon/src/util/metrics.ts emits firstPassApprovalPct on a 0..100 scale (Math.round(count/total*100), comment '// 0..100'). Both consumers multiply by 100 again: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MetricsPanel.kt:213 formats it * 100.0, and moe-vscode/src/providers/MetricsViewProvider.ts:295 does Math.round(pct * 100). A 50% rate shows as 5000%. Fix the consumers (keep the producer's documented 0..100 contract) and pin the contract with fixtures on both sides so the unit cannot drift again. Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 'Small corrections'.
definitionOfDone: MetricsPanel.kt renders firstPassApprovalPct 0/50/100 as 0%/50%/100% (JUnit test in moe-jetbrains covers all three values)
MetricsViewProvider.ts renders the same three values identically
metrics.ts has a vitest case asserting firstPassApprovalPct is 0..100 for a 1-of-2 first-pass fixture
docs/SCHEMA.md (or the metrics section of docs/MCP_SERVER.md) states the 0..100 unit explicitly
./gradlew test and daemon npm test green

implementationPlan.description: JetBrains first (primary IDE). TDD: write the failing test before touching the render code. Add a pure, headless-testable seam to MetricsPanel.kt — a `companion object { internal fun firstPassApprovalText(pct: Double?): String }` — mirroring the existing companion-seam convention proven by CreateTaskDialog.epicSelectionModel + CreateTaskDialogTest (JUnit 4, no Project/Application/Alarm needed). Step order: (1) create moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/MetricsPanelTest.kt asserting firstPassApprovalText(0.0)=="0%", (50.0)=="50%", (100.0)=="100%", and (null)=="—" (em dash, U+2014 — copy the exact glyph from MetricsPanel.kt line 213, do not retype a hyphen); (2) move the CURRENT expression `"%.0f%%".format(it * 100.0)` verbatim into the new companion function and bind line 213 to `firstPassValue.text = firstPassApprovalText(aggregate.firstPassApprovalPct)`; (3) run `./gradlew test` and RECORD the real numeric failures (expected 50%, got 5000%; expected 100%, got 10000%) — this is the epic-rail evidence that the test fails on the old behaviour, and a mere compile failure does not count; (4) delete only the `* 100.0`, leaving `"%.0f%%".format(it)`, and re-run green. Add a one-line comment above the companion function stating the daemon already emits percent units on 0..100 so consumers must not rescale. The null branch IS the missing-value error handling path and must keep returning the em dash unchanged; likewise leave the surrounding requestMetrics error handling (the swallowed-exception pooled-thread block above renderAggregate), locale handling, whole-number formatting, the hasAny empty-state logic, polling and every other KPI untouched. The tested function MUST be the one renderAggregate actually calls — an unused test-only helper is a rejection.

implementationPlan.description: VS Code consumer (trivial one-line fix, allowed in-task by the epic rail). The buggy formatter lives inside the inline webview script string, so the test must execute that emitted script rather than duplicate its math. Create moe-vscode/tests/metrics-view.test.cjs following the existing harness convention in tests/daemon-start.test.cjs (node:test + typescript transpileModule to CommonJS + node:vm, fake `vscode` module via the context require shim; npm test globs tests/*.test.cjs, so add no runner and no dependency). Build a MetricsViewProvider with a fake extensionUri and a fake MoeDaemonClient whose onMetrics/onConnectionChanged return `{ dispose() {} }`, then call the private renderer entry point `provider['getHtml']()` — it takes no arguments and tolerates a missing view (`this._view?.webview.cspSource ?? ''`). Extract the script with a `/<script>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/` match and THROW if it does not match. Run that script in a fresh vm context per fixture supplying: `acquireVsCodeApi: () => ({ postMessage() {} })`, a `document` with `querySelectorAll: () => []` and `getElementById: id => elements[id] ??= {}`, and a `window` whose addEventListener captures the 'message' handler (throw if no handler registered). Use bare `{}` stub elements so every DOM property the production script writes is absorbed implicitly by ordinary assignment — the test source must not name any DOM markup-injection property, since the repo forbidden-pattern rail greps for it. Drive the fixture by invoking that captured handler with `{ data: { type: 'aggregate', aggregate: { firstPassApprovalPct: N } } }` and assert elements.kpiFirstPass.textContent is exactly '0%', '50%', '100%' for N = 0/50/100, plus '—' for an omitted field, an explicit null, and a non-number — that typeof guard is the script's missing-value error handling and must survive the edit. Run the test BEFORE the fix and record the 5000%/10000% failures, then change line 295 `Math.round(a.firstPassApprovalPct * 100)` to `Math.round(a.firstPassApprovalPct)` and add the same 'daemon emits 0..100' comment. Missing script, missing handler and unexpected requires must all throw loudly rather than silently pass. Call provider.dispose() in a finally so no listener or poll timer leaks. Leave humaniseMs, escapeHtml, the range chips, the per-epic table and the connection-status error handling untouched.

implementationPlan.description: Pin the producer contract so the unit cannot drift back. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/metrics.test.ts (vitest, colocated like the other daemon *.test.ts files) importing the real computeMetricsAggregate and computeDashboardAggregate from './metrics.js'. Do NOT append to an existing test file and do NOT import any module that installs a hoisted vi.mock — a hoisted mock in the same file silently swallows appended cases (known repo gotcha). Build minimal deterministic Task fixtures with fixed ISO timestamps, cast through `as unknown as Task` so only the fields metrics.ts reads are required (status, epicId, metrics.rejectCount). Cases, all mutation-resistant exact-value assertions: two DONE tasks with metrics.rejectCount 0 and 1 give firstPassApprovalPct exactly 50 (not 0.5, not 5000) and the value is within 0..100; 0-of-2 gives exactly 0; 2-of-2 gives exactly 100; adding a non-DONE task with a rejectCount does not change the 50 result (it must not enter the approval denominator); computeDashboardAggregate over the same 1-of-2 input also reports exactly 50; and with no DONE tasks the raw aggregate is 0 while the dashboard field is undefined and absent after a JSON.stringify round-trip — that zero-vs-missing split is the producer's deliberate empty-input error handling and is what the IDE em dash depends on. These lock in already-correct behaviour, so they pass at baseline — that is expected; the fail-on-old-behaviour rail is carried by the two consumer tests. Change nothing in metrics.ts.

Leaks: firstPassApprovalText is pure with no mutable shared or static state; the VS Code test disposes the provider in a finally (releasing both metrics listeners and the 30s poll interval), the vm contexts are per-fixture and unreferenced afterwards, and readFileSync leaves no handle. DELIBERATE OUT-OF-SCOPE DECISION on hostile inputs, as the plan directs: this task restores the documented finite 0..100 contract ONLY. null/omitted is handled (em dash, both clients). Negative, NaN, Infinity and absurdly large values are unreachable through the documented producer contract (metrics.ts emits Math.round of a non-negative ratio*100, and JSON cannot even carry NaN/Infinity), so NO clamping, NaN guard or malformed-value policy was added; a hostile value would still print e.g. "NaN%" exactly as it did before this change. Two divergences noted and left alone for the same reason: Java's Formatter rounds HALF_UP while JS Math.round rounds half-up-toward-positive, differing only on negative half values, and the two disagree on formatting values above 1e21 — both unreachable because the wire value is always an integer 0..100. Locale: the Kotlin format string is unchanged, so digit rendering behaviour is exactly what shipped; a JVM default locale with non-Latin digits could theoretically make the new assertions fail, which is a property of the pre-existing formatter, not of this fix. Mutation resistance: restoring either multiplier demonstrably re-breaks the 50/100 assertions — that is precisely the recorded RED evidence from steps 1 and 2 (JetBrains expected:<50%> but was:<5000%> and expected:<100%> but was:<10000%>; VS Code '5000%' !== '50%' and '10000%' !== '100%') produced by these same unmodified test files. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Fix the consumers, keep the producer: metrics.ts already documents and emits 0..100 and moe.list_metrics is a published contract, so rescaling the producer would break the wire format and other readers. JetBrains uses a pure companion-object seam instead of bootstrapping an IntelliJ Application/Alarm fixture, because MetricsPanel needs a Project and the repo's JUnit 4 tests are headless (CreateTaskDialog already uses exactly this pattern). VS Code executes the emitted inline webview script in a vm with a tiny DOM stub rather than exporting a formatter and injecting Function.prototype.toString into the HTML (rename-fragile under esbuild) or asserting on source text (which passes even when rendering is broken). Inline fixtures per package avoid new shared fixture plumbing. Six steps / six files; the docs step is small because the unit is already documented and only needs an explicit prose sentence.
